# Use figma-diagrams

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Work with Figma and FigJam files via the Figma REST API — read existing file structure, list frames/pages, post comments, and produce FigJam-importable diagram specs.

**Reach for it when** the user mentions a Figma URL, asks to inspect/audit a Figma file, wants to comment on a design programmatically, or wants their architecture diagram in Figma.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install figma-diagrams                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install figma-diagrams --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install figma-diagrams --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Solution architect pack: [`--pack solution-architect`](../packs/use-the-solution-architect-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 and requests==2.34.2. What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/solution-architect/skills/figma-diagrams/manifest.json).

It needs `FIGMA_TOKEN` set in the environment.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "List the frames in our Figma file"
- "Read this Figma file structure via the API"
- "Post a comment on this Figma frame"
- "Convert this FigJam connector graph into a diagram spec"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Draw an architecture diagram in Mermaid from this description"
- "Reverse-engineer our architecture from the repo"
- "Build a PowerPoint deck from this content"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use figma-diagrams".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Never log the token.** Scripts use `os.environ["FIGMA_TOKEN"]`; don't pass it on the command line.
- **Don't dump 5 MB of JSON** to the user. Filter to pages/frames/groups (3 levels) and summarize.
- **Confirm before posting comments.** A comment is visible to anyone with file access — show the user the exact text and the file URL before calling `post_comment.py`.
- **Handle 429s.** The Figma API rate-limits (~25 req/min for some endpoints). If a script returns 429, back off and retry; don't loop.
